fail_closed_rules: SRN membership or proximity is a consultation/network-management input, not planning refusal or proof that a new access is acceptable
National Highways consultation or advice is not planning permission, highway works approval, land ownership or a section 278 agreement
an indicative highway boundary is not title ownership or a legal highway extent determination without authoritative boundary evidence
OS road-centreline or routing geometry is not the legal highway boundary, adoption status or access right
Major Road Network, Primary Route Network and Strategic Road Network classifications must not be collapsed into one legal or management regime
traffic-flow, speed or congestion observations are time-specific operational evidence, not proof of future development capacity
a Transport Assessment, Transport Statement or Travel Plan is evidence for decision-making, not a permission or guaranteed mitigation outcome
an agreed transport mitigation concept is not implemented infrastructure until the relevant legal agreement, design approval and works are complete
a stopping-up application, draft order or consultation is not a made order and does not extinguish highway rights
planning permission does not itself stop up or divert highway rights; the separate statutory order process remains required where applicable
route strategy, RIS3 project, funding programme or proposed scheme is not a constructed road, committed parcel access or planning permission
Active Travel England statutory consultation thresholds and guidance are consultation/design inputs, not automatic approval or refusal
active-travel design guidance is not evidence that a route is adopted, funded, deliverable or available over third-party land
proximity to railway infrastructure is not a development prohibition; proposal-specific safety, engineering and property rights must be assessed
Network Rail Asset Protection engagement or a BAPA is separate from planning permission, easement, wayleave, lease and other property rights
a Network Rail easement or property agreement does not replace asset-protection engineering approval, and vice versa
a level-crossing consultation trigger, order or mapped crossing is not proof of unacceptable risk or a planning refusal
ORR does not grant planning permission for development or automatically approve new or reinstated level crossings
HS2 safeguarding-area coverage is a referral/safeguarding control, not proof of acquisition, blight entitlement, refusal or current construction
Planning Data zero-record experimental HS2 safeguarding data must not be interpreted as absence of safeguarding; current DfT/HS2 maps control
Crossrail 2 safeguarding directions are route-protection evidence and must retain temporal/current-policy provenance rather than be treated as construction status
NaPTAN/public transport access-node points indicate transport access locations, not land ownership, service frequency, station capacity or walking-route feasibility
road, rail, active-travel, public-rights-of-way, planning, compulsory-purchase and property-right regimes remain separate unless an authoritative instrument links them
